title: Odile and the Tryouts
premise: Noor Fairweather, a debate champion trapped in a house where every conversation with his father ends in defeat, is counting down the days to graduation when his best friend Odile vanishes, leaving behind only a ring of keys to places Noor has never seen. Following the keys, Noor discovers Odile was secretly competing in an underground debate league whose champion earns a scholarship that could rewrite her future — and that she disappeared rather than throw a final match for a sponsor who owns her family's debts. As Noor takes her place in the tryouts, he must win two championships: the one on stage, and the invisible one at home, where love for his father wars with the duty to stop becoming him. In the end, Noor wins the title, exposes the sponsor, brings Odile home — not saved, but changed — and walks into graduation having finally won the argument that mattered.
about_author: Ansel Underhill is the pen name of a former high-school policy debater who spent four years losing arguments everywhere except at tournaments. They write young adult fiction about kids who are fluent in words but illiterate in their own hearts, and live somewhere with too many libraries and not enough silence.

chapters.title: The Countdown
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Opening day of senior spring semester; Noor tallies days left until graduation on a whiteboard in his room while rehearsing rebuttals against his father's expectations. Establishes the household as a debate he always loses. Emotional beat: weary defiance masking dread.

chapters.title: Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Odile misses their weekly diner ritual; her mother calls Noor in panic. At Odile's house Noor finds seven unfamiliar keys labeled in her handwriting with dates leading up to graduation. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: What Best Friends Don't Say
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, flashback woven through present search. Recalls six months of Odile's evasions — missed practices, unexplained cash, a bruise she called 'lockers.' Guilt blooms: he was counting days instead of noticing hers. Emotional beat: self-reproach.

chapters.title: First Key: The Laundromat
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The first key opens a storage cage behind a laundromat containing trophies engraved with names Noor doesn't recognize — including Odile's under an alias. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering a hidden life.

chapters.title: The Argument at Dinner
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. His father, a failed lawyer turned rigid accountant, demands Noor quit 'distractions' and focus on the state championship. Their fight escalates; Noor loses it exactly as predicted. Emotional beat: the familiar wound reopened.

chapters.title: Second Key: Room 12
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A key opens a motel room where someone has been living — Odile's handwriting on legal pads, flowcharts of arguments, a photo of Noor taped inside her notebook. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with alarm.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows Something
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (Odile's cousin). She reveals Odile competed in the Meridian League, an underground debate circuit where winners earn scholarships funded by shadowy sponsors. Marisol begs Noor to stay out. Emotional beat: warning delivered too late to matter.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. He attends Meridian tryouts using Odile's alias, telling himself it's reconnaissance. He wins his first round by accident of instinct. A scout named Voss marks his card. Emotional beat: intoxication of being seen.

chapters.title: Third Key: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Inside: evidence Odile was investigating the League itself — ledgers showing sponsors buying outcomes, debts attached to families like liens. Emotional beat: righteous anger kindling.

chapters.title: The Sponsor
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Introduces Aldous Renner, financier of the Meridian League, who collects 'futures' — scholarship contracts that bind winners to years of unpaid advocacy work. Voss admires and fears him. Emotional beat: elegant menace.

chapters.title: Fourth Key: Her Locker
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. School locker yields Odile's real notebook: she entered the League to erase her mother's debt, then stayed to burn it down. Final entry: 'If I win clean, they can't touch me. If I lose, don't look for me.' Emotional beat: heartbreak and resolve.

chapters.title: Losing at Home
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Father discovers Noor's absences, threatens to pull him from state championships. Noor, for once, doesn't argue back — he just leaves mid-sentence. Emotional beat: quiet rupture, first act of refusal.

chapters.title: Fifth Key: The Chapel
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A decommissioned chapel houses the League's finals venue. Noor watches a match from the balcony and sees how good the debaters are — and how afraid. Spots Odile's handwriting on the bracket wall. Emotional beat: awe laced with dread.

chapters.title: Partner
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A veteran Meridian debater adopts Noor as a partner, half-mentor, half-test. She knew Odile, warns that Renner lets investigators get close before he closes doors. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming.

chapters.title: Sixth Key: The Apartment That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Key opens a sublet rented under Noor's own name — Odile planned for him to follow her trail all along. He finds a letter: 'You're better than me at the thing that matters. Finish it.' Emotional beat: devastating trust.

chapters.title: State Semifinals
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor competes in the official state tournament on autopilot, winning while mentally running Meridian cases. Priya watches from the back. Emotional beat: hollow victory, divided self.

chapters.title: Renner Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Renner appears at the diner, urbane and generous, offering to clear Odile's mother's debt if Noor throws the Meridian final. He frames it as mercy. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya shows Noor the full ledger: dozens of families bound by Renner's contracts, including her own brother. Explains why no one testifies. Emotional beat: despair quantified.

chapters.title: Seventh Key: The Safe Deposit Box
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Last key opens a bank box containing notarized copies of Renner's contracts — Odile's insurance. A note says distribution requires a public platform: a championship stage, broadcast. Emotional beat: understanding the endgame.

chapters.title: Where Is Odile?
chapters.summary: Odile's POV (interleaved letters). Reveals Odile didn't vanish — she went dark deliberately, hiding with a retired League judge, gathering testimony, waiting for someone to finish what she started. Emotional beat: relief braided with fury at being used.

chapters.title: Father's File
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor finds his father's old bar card and a box of case files from the one case his father refused to throw — the loss that ended his career and hardened him. Emotional beat: seeing the enemy as a mirror.

chapters.title: The Real Argument
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Father and son have their first honest conversation: father admits he taught Noor to argue because he couldn't teach him to be safe. Neither wins. Emotional beat: grief becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: State Finals
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor wins the state championship decisively — the trophy his father always wanted — and feels nothing but momentum. Renner congratulates him publicly, tightening the trap. Emotional beat: triumph as fuel, not destination.

chapters.title: Qualifying Round
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Meridian semifinals; Noor debates brilliantly and cruelly, channeling his father's cutthroat style, and hates himself after. Priya calls him out. Emotional beat: identity crisis on stage.

chapters.title: Odile Comes Back Wrong
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Odile resurfaces briefly, gaunt and sharp-edged, furious that Noor followed the trail. She orders him out of the League. He refuses. Emotional beat: love expressed as conflict.

chapters.title: Her Side of It
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile explains going dark: witnesses die careers here, not bodies. She left keys because she trusted Noor's stubbornness more than his safety. Emotional beat: guilt confessed, forgiveness withheld.

chapters.title: The Judge Who Retired
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Meeting with the retired judge who shelters Odile; he confirms the contracts are enforceable and the only escape is public exposure — which requires the broadcast final. Emotional beat: plan crystallizing.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Renner, suspicious of Noor, has Voss dig up dirt: the alias, the stolen entry. Voss hesitates — first crack in loyalty. Emotional beat: complicity curdling.

chapters.title: Disqualified?
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Renner offers Noor a choice: forfeit eligibility or sign a contract like everyone else. Noor stalls by invoking League rules — debating his way into the final. Emotional beat: weaponized rules, rising stakes.

chapters.title: Priya's Price
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. To keep Noor eligible, Priya signs her own contract with Renner, sacrificing herself. She tells Noor afterward, daring him to make it worth it. Emotional beat: sacrifice as accusation.

chapters.title: Eighth Key: There Were Only Seven
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor realizes the eighth 'key' was metaphorical — Odile's note means the final key is the truth itself. He and Odile reconcile over the ledger, planning the broadcast exposure. Emotional beat: partnership restored.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Quiet chapter: Noor visits his father, asks him to be in the audience. Father says nothing, then shows up early with coffee. Emotional beat: fragile peace before the storm.

chapters.title: The Final, Part One
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Championship begins in the chapel, streamed per new League rules Renner regrets. Noor's opponent is Renner's handpicked champion. First exchange: Noor holds ground. Emotional beat: controlled fire.

chapters.title: The Final, Part Two
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Opponent pivots to personal attack — Odile's disappearance, Noor's fraud. Noor nearly shatters, then chooses honesty over polish, admitting everything on record. Emotional beat: authenticity as strategy.

chapters.title: The Rebuttal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax: Noor uses his rebuttal to read the contract terms aloud, naming families, naming Renner, as the stream runs. Judges must rule on substance; the audience hears everything. Emotional beat: the argument that matters, won.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Renner's empire cracks — a judge voids contracts, Voss testifies, Priya's contract burns. Renner exits without apology, already composing his next venture. Emotional beat: victory incomplete but real.

chapters.title: Odile Decides
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Offered reinstatement and glory, Odile declines the League entirely, choosing community college and her mother's freed future. She and Noor part as something truer than best friends. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Whiteboard reads zero. Father hands Noor the old bar card — 'you'll need it more than me.' Noor crosses the stage to thin applause and full heart. Emotional beat: arrival without fanfare.

chapters.title: The Argument He Keeps Winning
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. Fall: Noor preps for pre-law, coaches novice debaters, keeps the seventh key on his keyring. Final line reframes the theme: some arguments you win once and spend forever defending. Emotional beat: earned hope.
